title: Shared definitions for the CoS-first 1.2 contracts
description: B0 of spec v0.3 (planning-studio INIT-2026-0007, 15_SPEC_1_2_COS_FIRST_v0.3), section 4.1 and 4.2. Every other schema in this folder references these definitions.

timestamp.description: ISO 8601 with an explicit offset. Naive local times are never written: the writer knows its zone.

tz.description: An IANA zone. 1.2 writes America/Chicago; the field stays so a reader never guesses.

data_scope.description: Section 4.1. Whose data. In 1.2 the only value written is personal. company:<id> and client:<id> are reserved names: a 1.2 writer refuses them and a reader refuses a record carrying them.

data_scope_reserved.description: The reserved names, for documentation and for readers' refusal messages. Never written in 1.2.

environment.description: Section 4.1. Which deployment. Kept apart from data_scope and from a credential's permissions.

id.description: A stable identifier: letters, digits, and . _ : @ - only (@ joins an obligation or episode id to its date).

digest.description: sha256 over canonical JSON: sorted keys, separators (',', ':'), UTF-8, ensure_ascii false.

typed_ref.description: Section 4.1. A typed canonical reference: what kind of record, which one, which revision of it.

source_instance.description: Section 4.1. Which host and service wrote the record.

provenance.description: Section 4.2, R-7. Rooms' CONTEXT_CLASSES (rooms/store.py:34) plus domain_fact and approved. One vocabulary for Rooms and the CoS store.

attributed_text.description: Section 4.2. Text with its provenance. robert_source needs the verbatim turn it came from; domain_fact needs its canonical record; approved needs where Robert accepted it. The server sets robert_source, never the model.

seat.description: Section 4.14. Bound server-side from the session, never named by the model.

origin.description: Section 4.14. Why the action happened. scheduled is lane one only; lane two needs its harness trigger.

who.description: Section 4.6. Who owes an obligation. A domain name stands for that domain's owner.

reader_state.description: Section 4.7. Every reader answers one of these. stale carries the last good value and its as_of.

envelope.description: Section 4.1. The identity every stored record carries.
